summary.headline: Gabriel India consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to INR1,608 crore, with EBITDA up 12% to INR141 crore at an 8.8% margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 23% YoY to INR1,608 crore in Q2 FY27 and EBITDA rose 12% to INR141 crore (8.8% margin), with H1 revenue up 19% to INR3,034 crore. Standalone revenue grew 23% to INR1,399 crore but standalone PBT before exceptionals rose only 7% to INR89 crore, with margin pressure from commodity, logistics and forex issues. The quarter included a new seating JV with FORVIA (signed 6 Oct 2026, incorporated 19 Oct 2026, Gabriel 50% less one share) and a partial quarter of HL Mando Anand, which closed on 11 Sep 2026. Management declared an interim dividend of INR2.15 per share and said capex will run at INR1,000-1,500 crore a year on a consolidated basis.

segments.name: Standalone suspension (PV, CV, 2W, 3W)
segments.commentary: Standalone growth was supported by core suspension demand. Management said CV growth matched the industry because Gabriel holds more than 85% share. PV lagged the market in Q2 due to a mix issue, with smaller cars growing faster and Gabriel's models underperforming.

segments.name: Fluid business (Anchemco, restructured into standalone)
segments.commentary: Anchemco was added to standalone after restructuring and contributed to revenue growth. Management said urea-linked raw material costs rose again in Q2, so price recovery from customers lagged.

segments.name: Sunroof
segments.commentary: Q2 was hit by a fire at a Hyundai supplier that disrupted Hyundai/Kia volumes. The BAYON launch began, with panoramic roofs expected to be 75-80% of its business and about 100,000 cars a year (60% India, 40% exports).

segments.name: Equity-accounted JVs/associates (Dana Anand, Henkel Anand, SK Enmove Gabriel, HL Mando Anand, HL Klemove)
segments.commentary: Share of PBT was INR48 crore in Q2 and INR91 crore in H1. HL Mando Anand and HL Klemove contributed only a few days in Q2 and will reflect fully from Q3. Management said Henkel's PAT margin was pressured by commodity and logistics costs, while Dana was offset by export forex gains.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated capex expected to run at INR1,000-1,500 crore a year.

FORVIA seating JV closing targeted by December 2026 end. The business to be transferred is the frame business, about INR150 crore in size (against a stated INR250 crore run-rate at 10% margin for the total Faurecia India seating business), with mechanisms excluded.
HL Mando Anand and HL Klemove to reflect on a full-quarter basis from Q3 FY27.
Management reaffirmed the INR50,000 crore Vision 2030 group revenue target and said the 2026 industry growth has brought it closer to that target.
Management expects Creta to phase out in FY28 with only the Creta EV continuing. AI4 SOP is expected next year, and bids are pending with Tata and Mahindra.
Management expects HL Klemove ROCE, currently below 10%, to trend toward the company average at steady state.
capex_capacity: Consolidated capex guided at INR1,000-1,500 crore a year, covering capacity, a new plant and plant improvements.
New seating JV plant to be set up, with Chennai as the planned location and Pune also cited.
Sunroof Phase 1 is operating. BC4i and BC4T are in commercial production, and AI4 is due next year. Capacity expansion for new wins depends on customer and could be capex or relocation.
Anchemco's contribution is small relative to the group, per management.
demand_pricing: Industry (Q2 FY27 production growth): 2W +16.5%, PV +25%, CV +34%, 3W +24%. H1 growth: 2W +19.5%, PV +21%, CV +25%, 3W +30.5%.
Standalone PV shock absorber share declined in H1 because Gabriel's models in the small-car segment did not keep pace with the market.
Commodity and logistics costs have squeezed price-cost recovery across subsidiaries. Management said Anchemco's urea-linked costs rose again in Q2.
2W EV: Gabriel started supplies to Bajaj Chetak in Oct 2026, and management said the order book is strong.
Seating JV product value is expected at INR30,000-50,000 per passenger car set, with mechanisms about 15-20% of seat value.
Sunroof: AYI did not ramp as expected. Hyundai fire-related disruption affected Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Which growth route (organic, new JVs, acquisitions, product expansion) will matter most toward the INR50,000 crore Vision 2030 target, and what return thresholds apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the HL Klemove and FORVIA seating JVs as key steps and said ADAS and seating are high-value product areas. It did not give numbers or formal return thresholds, but said it does not compromise on ROI.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Henkel's PAT margin volatile and is it seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not seasonal. Commodity and logistics costs have outpaced customer price recovery across businesses. Dana is offset by export forex gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the seating JV scope, and how much of content per vehicle sits outside it?
qa_highlights.answer: The JV will be the single point of contact for the full seating system. Mechanisms, about 15-20% of seat content, will be bought from FORVIA's 100%-owned Indian mechanism company. FORVIA's seating business in India moves into the JV except mechanisms.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an anchor order for the seating JV and is a royalty payable?
qa_highlights.answer: The JV takes over existing won business, including a Volkswagen program. Value will be disclosed after closing. A royalty will be paid for technology from the Indian R&D centre, which management called normal for such deals.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PV shock absorber and CV revenue growth trail the market?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Jaggi said CV growth matched the market given more than 85% share, with aftermarket and railway lumped into CV numbers. PV lagged mainly because of mix, with small-car models underperforming.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sunroof volume position, and what is the outlook for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is improving versus last year. BC4i, BC4T and BAYON are ramping, AI4 comes next year, and Creta phases out in FY28 except for the EV version. Bids are pending with Tata and Mahindra.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and margin perimeter for the Faurecia seating business transfer?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing is targeted for December end. The frame business, about INR150 crore in size, transfers at its current margin. Mechanisms are excluded.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth expectations for HL Mando and HL Klemove?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects both to grow above the market. HL Mando is about 60-65% Hyundai/Kia and is adding Tata, Maruti Suzuki and Mahindra. HL Klemove is already with Hyundai, Tata and Mahindra, and is adding Maruti Suzuki.

risks_watch: Persistent commodity, logistics and forex pressure on price-cost recovery, which is visible in standalone PBT margin falling to 6.3% and in the Henkel and Anchemco margins.
PV small-car share loss, with H1 PV shock absorber share lagging the market.
Sunroof concentration on Hyundai/Kia, the Creta phase-out in FY28, and AI4 ramp timing.
Seating JV execution: closing by December 2026, plant build in Chennai and Pune, and disclosure of order book value after closing.
HL Klemove ROCE below 10% during the ramp-up phase.
Dividend and capex funding, given the INR1,000 crore NCD at 8.15%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategic pipeline and the festive-season demand backdrop. Notably cautious and evasive on margins, sunroof outlook and JV financial specifics, deferring numbers to post-closing.

key_quotes: The joint venture will focus on developing, manufacturing, supplying seat frames and complete seating systems for passenger vehicle, where Gabriel India will be holding 50% less 1 share and FORVIA will be holding 50% plus 1 share.
So there's no seasonality. It's only -- I think the business globally are impacted across India, all because of the commodity changes.

So, I think this commercial vehicle, there is no degrowth. The growth purely on the CV side is exactly matching the industry growth because obviously, with the --more than 85% market share, that is bound to be in line with the market.
I think we are targeting to complete the closing by December end.
So we expect that our capex should be always running between INR1,000 crores to INR1,500 crores on a consolidation basis.
Yes, of course. As I said, generally, these are -- we don't compromise on the ROI. It is a temporary phase because of the investment already done.

growth.why: Consolidated Q2 revenue grew 23% and H1 19%, with Vision 2030 INR50,000 crore target reaffirmed and capex of INR1,000-1,500 crore a year guided, but the brief gives no explicit forward revenue growth number and capacity backing is partial (Chennai/Pune seating plant unscheduled, AI4 next year, HL Mando and HL Klemove full-quarter effect from Q3).
